works.title: A Probabilistic Proof of a Positivstellensatz of Baldi-Sinn-Telek-Weigert
works.abstract: The AI gives a probabilistic proof of a uniform-denominator Positivstellensatz of Baldi--Sinn--Telek--Weigert for Laurent polynomials whose induced homogeneous form is strictly positive on the nonnegative part of a projective toric variety. Only this abstract was human-written. Three classical tools from mathematical statistics and probability theory were used by the AI: the Barndorff-Nielsen completion of discrete exponential families, sufficiency-based invariance under exponential tilting following Halmos--Savage and Van Campenhout--Cover, and the conditional limit theorem (equivalence of ensembles) of Diaconis--Freedman.
works.subject: math.AG

works.title: A nontrivial critical window for autocatalytic emergence in the binary polymer model
works.abstract:
The limiting probability is determined for a reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) set in two reversible binary-polymer models. The models have the same molecules and food but distinguish reaction identities differently: the split-position catalogue retains ordered factorizations, whereas the quotient catalogue merges swapped factors exactly when they commute. With independent molecule--reaction catalysis, one mark shared by both directions, and mean catalysis $f_n$ per molecule satisfying $f_n/n	o\lambda>0$, the RAF probability converges in either model to $\Theta_
u(\lambda)=S_
u(1-e^{-\lambda}),\qquad 
u\in\{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{qt}\},$ where $S_
u$ is the survival probability of infinite ordinary reversible food closure in the corresponding independent open-reaction field. Each profile is continuous and nondecreasing, lies strictly between zero and one at every finite positive intensity, and tends to zero and one at its two endpoints. Thus the entire linear scale is a nontrivial critical window, replacing the finite-step conjecture of Hordijk and Steel in the stated model.

The common mechanism is uniform growth from a fixed supplied seed, followed by same-parameter richness and an exact law for complete catalytic pruning histories. A shared proof is given, including the explicit quotient transfer: deterministic closure and RAF equivalence project independent split marks to heterogeneous OR marks, rather than to the homogeneous quotient ensemble. The profiles satisfy $\Theta_\mathrm{sp}(\lambda/2)\le\Theta_\mathrm{qt}(\lambda)\le\Theta_\mathrm{sp}(\lambda)$; productive food gateways give the conventional bounds $\Theta_\mathrm{sp}(\lambda)\le1-e^{-32\lambda}$ and $\Theta_\mathrm{qt}(\lambda)\le1-e^{-30\lambda}$. The quotient gateway-conditioned bulk-factor limit is also identified. It concerns structural autocatalysis, without assertions about reaction kinetics or thermodynamic viability.

works.title: A Formally Verified Certificate Proof of the Maximum Number of Stable Matchings for Six Men and Six Women
works.abstract: We give a complete Lean 4 verification of the theorem that the maximum number of stable matchings for six men and six women with strict complete preferences is f(6)=48. Jo (2026) previously proved the unrestricted upper bound, and Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger (1995) supplied an attaining construction. Our contribution is an alternative, fully formalized proof using a finite certificate; the value 48 and the unrestricted theorem are already known. We reduce stable matchings of arbitrary profiles to order ideals of sequences of cyclic partner exchanges in which no man revisits a partner. A weighted frontier recurrence counts these ideals, and a sum of permanents bounds every future continuation. These bounds yield a finite certificate with 135,828 states. The complete argument, including the reduction for arbitrary profiles, certificate soundness, all concrete checks, and an attaining profile, has been formalized and checked in Lean 4. The final unconditional theorem depends only on the standard axioms of Lean and mathlib.

works.title: Pattern-avoiding binary arrays and a Stirling-type table: explicit formulas, exact recurrence orders, and non-D-finiteness
works.abstract: Let $a_k(n)$ be the number of $n\times k$ binary arrays in which no row contains $001$ or $010$ and no column contains $001$ or $011$ as three consecutive entries (OEIS A207123). Splitting the rows by parity gives $a_k(n)=U_k(\lceil n/2\rceil)\,U_k(\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$, where $U_k(m)$ counts sequences in $\{0,\dots,m\}^k$ in which every three consecutive entries $(a,b,c)$ satisfy $b=c$ or $a\ge\max(b,c)$; equivalently, $U_k(m)$ counts the multichains of length $m$ in a subposet $\Lambda_k$ of the Boolean lattice. We prove three main results. First, for each $m$ the minimal order of a linear recurrence in $k$ is exactly $3m+1$, and a unique factorization into blocks gives a positive double-sum formula for $U_k(m)$ in terms of Stirling and $r$-Stirling numbers. Second, the bivariate generating function is not D-finite, and every polynomial-coefficient recurrence that holds on a quadrant is a left multiple of the defining four-term recurrence; the same holds for an associated Stirling-type triangle $N(k,q)$, and $U$ is not Stirling-like in the sense of Kauers. Third, the numerators $h_k(t)$ of $\sum_mU_k(m)t^m=h_k(t)/(1-t)^{k+1}$, analogues of the Eulerian polynomials, have only simple real zeros; equivalently, the chain polynomials of the posets $\Lambda_k$ are real-rooted, and the rows of $N$ are log-concave. We also determine all binomial shapes with nonnegative parameters in which $U_k(m)$ is a single sum, and show that the near-diagonal entries $N(k,k-d)$ are polynomials in $k$ starting exactly at $k=2d+2$. The reduction, the exact orders, the explicit formula, the non-D-finiteness, the description of the quadrant recurrences and the near-diagonal theorem are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

works.title: Gallai's conjecture with two exceptional even vertices
works.abstract:
Gallai conjectured that every connected finite simple graph on n vertices admits an edge partition into at most ⌈n/2⌉ simple paths. Botler and Sambinelli proved this when every even-degree vertex has at most three even neighbours. Fan, Hou and Zhou exempted one designated even vertex of positive degree and ensured that at least two paths ended there. Xie obtained the same endpoint conclusion for either of two adjacent designated even vertices, in separate partitions, when every other even vertex has at most three even neighbours.

We prove that the same endpoint conclusion holds without requiring the two designated even vertices to be adjacent. Let F be the subgraph induced by the even-degree vertices of a connected finite simple graph G on n vertices, and let h and x be distinct vertices of F. Suppose every other vertex of F has degree at most three in F. Then for each of h and x there is an edge partition into at most ⌈n/2⌉ simple paths, at least two of which end at that vertex. Consequently, Gallai's bound holds whenever at most two vertices of F have degree greater than three.

The two choices may use different partitions. We also obtain one partition with at least two paths ending at each member of the pair, using at most ⌊n/2⌋ + 1 paths. At odd order this is Gallai's bound. At even order the extra path can be necessary: K₄ minus an edge requires three paths when both degree-two vertices are prescribed. The ceiling and endpoint bounds are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib and registered as PALOMAR-2026-10-04-000006, version 1.

works.title: Fixed-Level TQFT Transport of Marked Handleslide Coherence:  Disjoint Cubes and a Three-Handle Pentagon
works.abstract:
Fix an ordinary level $K\geq1$ and a fully specified family of pairwise disjoint positive handleslides on a compression body.  The main question is how a literal geometric relation becomes a literal finite-level operator relation.  We construct a finite reduced skein fibre and one normalized isomorphism
$$
  Q_{K,d}:\mathcal M_{K,d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal V^+_{K,d}
$$
to the corresponding scalar-extended Walker--TQFT state space.  Reusing this map at every vertex sends the supplied weight-zero slide cylinders to $E_K$-linear automorphisms: geometric squares become operator squares, finite slide orders give the same operator, and forward/reverse maps telescope for all declared phases and integer weights.  The construction is fibrewise and makes no comparison between levels.  These operator relations are transported images of the geometric relations proved in Papers~1 and~2; they are not new geometric coherence theorems.

We then treat a fully specified positive three-handle pentagon.  Its vertex-zero compression body admits a compatible fixed-level comparison core: a rational disk-kernel cap, a normalized complementary handlebody, a reduced spine model, and one universal-construction isomorphism $Q_{K,d}^{\mathfrak q}:\mathcal M_{K,d}^{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal V^+_{K,d}$. The geometric weight-zero Walker pentagon consequently has a literal operator image over \(E_K\), with explicit inverse formulas and a fixed-basis matrix corollary.  Different comparison cores are related by a typed comparison groupoid and give intertwined operator systems; no canonical comparison or literal equality between different coordinate choices is asserted.

works.title: Integral tail signatures and the Hilbert--Smith conjecture
works.abstract: The obstruction to an effective $p$-adic manifold action is an integer signature tail. On asymptotically controlled rational modules over one fixed free $C_p$-space, finite-cover Mayer--Vietoris makes the difference between $p$ copies and quotient-permutation tensoring nilpotent. Every degree-four class therefore has eventually $p$-divisible signatures. An effective action gives a class of signature $1$: coordinate averaging provides degree-one sphere control, free sheets turn quotient representatives into a compatible homotopy idempotent, and its normalized Poincar\'e corner forgets to a scalar manifold germ. Successive localization boundaries recover one copy of $\CP^2$, up to sign. The resulting contradiction proves the Hilbert--Smith conjecture.

works.title: Linchpin Theorems
works.abstract:
A proof assistant checks a formal proposition. It does not check that the
proposition expresses the mathematics that its author intended. This
distinction becomes pressing when large bodies of mathematics are
autoformalized. We propose the use of linchpin theorems: statements
whose meanings can be audited with relatively little mathematical
infrastructure, and whose proofs connect them to substantial results.
Examples range from sphere packing and the classification of Lie algebras
to regularity theory, the Weil conjectures, and computational complexity.

works.title: Almost all Markoff numbers are unique.
works.abstract:
A Markoff number is the largest coordinate of a positive integer solution of
$a^2+b^2+c^2=3abc$. Frobenius conjectured in 1913 that every Markoff number
is the largest coordinate of exactly one such solution with $a\le b\le c$.
We prove that the conjecture holds for almost all Markoff numbers: the
proportion of exceptions among the Markoff numbers up to $X$ tends to $0$
as $X\to\infty$.

Two such solutions with the same largest coordinate give simple closed
geodesics of equal length on the modular torus, that is, primitive homology
classes $v,w$ with equal values $N(v)=N(w)$ of the McShane--Rivin stable
norm $N$. Estimates for the boundary of the unit ball of $N$ reduce the
problem to the equations $N(Gv)=N(v)$ with $G$ a rational linear map. For
each $G$ that is not a symmetry of the torus, a zero-one law for the
$3$-adic analytic dynamics of the mapping class group on the Markoff
surface shows that the solutions $v$ have density zero.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: One of  β(4), β(6),..., β(36) is irrational
works.abstract: Let $\beta(s)=\sum_{m\ge 0}(-1)^m(2m+1)^{-s}$ be Dirichlet's beta function. We prove that at least one of the seventeen numbers $\beta(4),\beta(6),\dots,\beta(36)$ is irrational. All previous explicit results of this kind that we know of include $\beta(2)$, Catalan's constant; our statement does not involve $\beta(2)$ at all. The proof uses the linear forms $L_n=\sum_{t\ge0}(-1)^tR_n''(t)$ attached to a very-well-poised rational function $R_n$ with triple integer zeros and half-integer poles. The second derivative, a $\beta$-analogue of a device of Rivoal, removes $\beta(2)$, and a symmetry removes the odd values. The zeros of $R_n$ run through the region of its poles, which makes every prime $p>n$ harmless. The common denominators are controlled by a $p$-adic analysis and an arithmetic integral that we bound with an exact rational certificate. The size of $L_n$ is bounded by an elementary estimate on the real axis, and its nonvanishing for infinitely many $n$ follows from a saddle-point analysis along a certified contour. The whole proof, including every numerical certificate, has been formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib and checked by the Lean kernel, using only Lean's three standard axioms.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Finite Valuation Words and Terminal Obstructions for the Accelerated Syracuse Map
works.abstract: We develop a finite-word obstruction framework for the accelerated Syracuse map on positive odd integers. A finite valuation word determines an exact iterate formula and a unique realization class modulo a power of two; compatible infinite prefixes define a natural two-adic inverse-limit object together with least positive representatives. The first part records the exact finite-word congruence machinery, finite-descent equivalence, terminal-surplus identity, terminal-ceiling break criterion, bad-prefix windows, activated density collapse, stabilization criterion, and strict-jump bookkeeping. The second part uses these tools to isolate terminal obstruction classes for a hypothetical counterexample: a bounded branch leading to a nontrivial accelerated cycle, and an unbounded eventual no-jump branch, successively reduced through a chain of geometric and combinatorial normal forms to a packet-surplus compensation target. The resulting reduction spine is lossless: Collatz follows from exclusion of nontrivial accelerated cycles together with a packet-surplus, or stronger record-ladder, compensation theorem for the unbounded branch. As a closed module, we include a closed class-exclusion theorem showing that no eventually periodic infinite low-surplus valuation chain is realized by a positive odd integer. On the bounded branch, we further record, as an explicit unproved roadmap step, that the terminal-ceiling strict-jump obstruction reduces to a single recurrent valuation-mismatch statement. This manuscript proves the architecture stated in its theorems, propositions, lemmas, and corollaries; it states the remaining terminal exclusions explicitly as problems, conjectures, or roadmap steps, and does not claim a completed proof of the full Collatz conjecture.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: A fourteen-dimensional biperfect Lie bialgebra
works.abstract:
We construct a fourteen-dimensional Lie bialgebra for which both the
underlying Lie algebra and its dual are perfect. The construction is
defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ and is self-dual over $\mathbb{C}$. It gives an affirmative
answer to Question 4.1(3) of Etingof--Gelaki--Guralnick--Saxl, arXiv:9912068.
Its twenty-eight-dimensional Drinfeld double is quasitriangular with
injective cobracket, also answering Question 4.1(4).
works.subject: math.QA

works.title: A universal group with thirteen relators
works.abstract: We construct a finitely presented group with 13 relators that contains an isomorphic copy of every finitely presented group. This improves Valiev's bound of 21 relators for universal groups. The proof combines Valiev's construction, subgroup calculations of Kegel--Li--Ren, and small-cancellation theory.
works.subject: math.GR

works.title: An elliptic curve of rank $\geq 34$ and root number $-1$ over a quadratic field
works.abstract: In this article, we find a quadratic twist over $\mathbb{Q}$ of rank  $\geq 2$ (and $\geq 3$ assuming parity) of an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ of rank $\geq 32$, recently found by Elkies, Klagsbrun, and Li. We use a family of quadratic twists of rank $\geq 2$ over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ constructed by Mestre to search for twists $E^D$ with root number $-1$, computing all root numbers without factoring the (very large) twisting parameter $D$. As a result, we exhibit an explicit integer $D$, with $411$ digits (a square times an integer with $381$ digits), such that $E^D$ has root number $-1$ and two independent rational points. In particular, the rank of $E$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ is at least $34$, unconditionally, and at least $35$ if we assume the Parity Conjecture.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Rational Fourth Powers Summing to 82
works.abstract: We prove that the only primitive positive integer solutions of $x^4+y^4=82z^4$ are $(1,3,1)$ and $(3,1,1)$. An arithmetic reduction lifts every other putative solution to an elliptic curve over $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{41},\sqrt{2})$. An explicit 2-descent determines its rank as 3. A logarithmic functional then excludes all nonzero parameters in the relevant 2-adic disc, including both relative sign patterns at the two places above 2. The same argument determines every point of the auxiliary quartic whose parameter is rational: only the two points at infinity occur. Exact square identities also determine the quotient modulo 2, prove that the displayed subgroup has odd index, and give the vanishing of the 2-primary part of the Tate–Shafarevich group. Two reductions determine the torsion. The finite arithmetic certificates are supplied in two self-contained Python programs; no height cutoff or conjectural rank computation is used.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: The P\'olya--Vinogradov inequality with $\log\log q$
works.abstract:
We prove unconditionally that every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q\ge3$ has
character sums of size at most $C\sqrt q\log\log q$. Montgomery and Vaughan proved this bound under
the generalised Riemann hypothesis, and Paley showed that it is optimal. The proof uses the
zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$, which also gives $|L'/L(1,\chi)|\ll\log\log q$ and two-sided
bounds for the Euler--Kronecker constants of the cyclotomic fields $\mathbb Q(\zeta_q)$.

works.title: The Willow Transform and the Blind Zone Theorem: A Sharp Information-Theoretic Obstruction in the Turán Hierarchy for the Riemann xi-Function
works.abstract:
Let Xi(t) = xi(1/2 + it) be the Riemann Xi-function, let
Xi(t) = sum_{k>=0} (-1)^k c_k t^{2k} be its even Taylor
expansion at the origin, and let D(n,r) = det[c_{n+i-j}]
(i,j = 0..r-1) be the Toeplitz minors whose positivity for
all n >= 0, r >= 1 is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis
(RH). We prove a sharp and quantitative obstruction in the
resulting hierarchy of criteria.

Parametrising the zeros of G(z) = sum c_k z^k by
beta_j = -1/z_j, we establish by the dual Jacobi-Trudi
identity the exact identity D(n,r) = s_{(r^n)}(beta), the
Schur function of the rectangular partition (r^n) in the
variables beta. A zero of zeta off the critical line
contributes to beta a conjugate pair rho e^{+-i theta} whose
angle theta is exactly the vertical angle of the violating
pair of zeros, while zeros on the critical line contribute
positive real variables. For two variables we prove the
closed form

s_{(a,b)}(rho e^{i theta}, rho e^{-i theta})
    = rho^{a+b} sin((a+1-b) theta) / sin theta
    = rho^{a+b} U_{a-b}(cos theta),

U_k being the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind, so
that the sign is governed by the classical criterion
U_k(cos theta) > 0 if and only if (k+1) theta < pi.

Since a Schur function in two variables can be expanded
through the coproduct s_lambda(X sqcup Y) = sum_mu s_mu(X)
s_{lambda/mu}(Y), and since s_mu(X) > 0 for positive real X,
positivity reduces to the two-variable factors, whose index
k = a - b is bounded by the number of columns r, not by the
shift n. This yields:

Blind Zone Theorem. If a violating pair subtends a vertical
angle theta < pi/(r+1), then every Toeplitz minor D(n,r')
with r' <= r is strictly positive, notwithstanding the
presence of non-real zeros.

The critical strip together with gamma_1 = 14.134725141...
forces theta <= theta_max = 2 arctan(1/(2 gamma_1)) =
0.07071826... rad, whence pi/theta_max = 44.424... and
therefore every order r <= 43 is completely
non-discriminating.

We emphasise that the exponential bound is on the order r
and not on the shift n; we exhibit the mechanism and show
the contrary n-based bound is false. We also record the
refutation of a "universal covering law" previously
conjectured by the author, and a floating-point artefact
that nearly produced a false refutation of the main theorem.

No claim of a proof of RH is made.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Linear Trace-Deficit Decay for Permanents of Positive Semidefinite Contractions
works.abstract: Every Hermitian positive semidefinite contraction \(A\) satisfies \(\operatorname{per}(A)\leq\exp(-\operatorname{tr}(I-A)/68)\). This proves the linear trace-deficit bound conjectured by Ebrahimnejad, Nagda, and Oveis Gharan, whose estimate had quadratic dependence on the normalized deficit. The proof combines a size-biased complex Gaussian representation, a block version of Hanson–Wright decoupling, and a rational Loewner majorant. The constant is uniform in the dimension and is not optimized.
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: A finite-delay code for lexicographic graph products
works.abstract: For all finite simple graphs, the strong product and both ordered lexicographic products have the same Shannon capacity, answering a question of Sason. An explicit code conversion delays one component by a single block, with rate loss tending to zero. The equality extends to arbitrary mixtures of the two products and survives adjoining an additional strong-product factor.
works.subject: math.IT

works.title: Sharp fractional Helly bounds for common affine flats
works.abstract: If an $\alpha$ fraction of the $(d-k+1)$-tuples of closed convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ have an intersection containing a whole affine $k$-flat, then a fraction $1-(1-\alpha)^{1/(d-k+1)}$ of the sets share such a flat. This coefficient is best possible, resolving the sharp fractional De Santis question of Ludwigson and Soberón. The geometric result behind the bound is $(d-k)$-collapsibility of the common-flat complex, proved by coordinating convex sweeps in varying quotient spaces.
works.subject: math.MG

works.title: The rank-one Dixmier conjecture for elements of mass at most six
works.abstract: Let K be a field of characteristic zero and let P,Q in A_1(K) satisfy [Q,P]=1. We prove that P,Q generate A_1(K) if either has mass at most six, meaning at most six nonzero homogeneous components for the grading deg X=1, deg Y=-1, with no degree bound on either element. This extends the four-component theorem of Guccione, Guccione and Valqui. The proof combines their Newton-polygon restrictions with a classification of polynomial pairs r,f satisfying an associated scalar differential equation under the condition that r^2 has at most six monomial terms. The scalar argument uses a two-dimensional Vandermonde kernel, Rolle's theorem, and a sign and parity obstruction. The scalar classification and the mass bound reduce the crossing cases to a binomial-power face. We exclude that face using at most one Newton cut, without a mass bound on the transformed pair. We also exclude a family of pure-power crossing faces with prime outer exponent, without a mass bound. A seven-term scalar solution shows that the scalar classification is sharp, although its associated Weyl face is excluded by the pure-power theorem. Theorem 1.1 is formalized in Lean 4 and registered as Palomar entry PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000006, version 2.
works.subject: math.RA

works.title: Diameter-Free Pointwise Gaussian KDE in Near-Additive Query Time
works.abstract: Wagner asked whether Gaussian kernel density estimation in $\mathbb R^d$ admits query time $\widetilde O(d+\varepsilon^{-2})$ without dependence on the diameter of the data. We answer this affirmatively for each fixed query: a randomized data structure answers a query to additive error $\varepsilon$ with probability $1-\delta$ in time $O((d+\varepsilon^{-2})\log(d+1)\log(2/\delta))$, independently of the number of data points and of their diameter. The key ingredient is a variance bound for a Fastfood-type structured Fourier block that holds uniformly in the norm of the displacement.
works.subject: cs.DS

works.title: Finite Projective Source Geometry for GL2: Abel Resolvents and Central-Jet Degree Laws
works.abstract:
Starting from the two trace functions p1 = Tr(A) and p2 = Tr(A^2) for semisimple A in GL2(C), we develop the associated projective source geometry. The coordinate y = t^2/d - 1 identifies the adjoint character, and normalized Haar measure on a specified closed subgroup H of SO(3) pushes forward to a probability measure nu_H. We describe this measure through harmonic multiplicities, moments, and its Stieltjes transform, and prove that it determines H up to conjugacy within the closed-subgroup class of SO(3).

A positive Abel kernel resums the projective character tower and gives a resolvent formula whose endpoint limit recovers the mass of the identity atom. We give explicit Abel transforms for the finite rotation groups and positive-dimensional benchmark sources, and derive a finite-image Frobenius-prime Abel limit from Chebotarev. For central-jet interpolation, we prove two exact degree laws: the cyclic-versus-torus minimum degree is max(n, M+1), while the normalized tetrahedral detector against S4 and A5 has minimum degree 3 for M = 1, 2 and M+2 for M >= 3. We also compute the integral image of the tetrahedral averaging functional, obtaining 2Z for every M >= 2.

All results are stated with their hypotheses. The paper does not claim a general infinite-spectrum Beyond Endoscopy trace formula or transfer of central-jet vanishing to orbital kernels.
works.subject: math.RT

works.title: Fractional DAG treewidth controls DAG treewidth: profile reorientation and VC-dimension rounding
works.abstract: For a nonempty finite graph, let \(F\) be its fractional DAG treewidth, maximized over all acyclic orientations. Its DAG treewidth is at most \(160F^3\ln(16F)\). This answers the boundedness question of Bressan, Lanzinger, and Roth. Reorienting the graph converts shattered source profiles into projective-plane obstructions, which bound their VC dimension by \(5F^2\). Classical epsilon-net rounding then converts fractional bag covers to integral ones without changing the decomposition.
works.subject: cs.DM

works.title: The Coloured Sand Theorem: the p-part of the sandpile group of the Hamming graph, for every prime p dividing q and every dimension d
works.abstract: Let $H(d,q)=K_q^{d}$ be the Hamming graph and $K(H(d,q))$ its sandpile group (critical group, Jacobian). For primes $p\nmid q$ its $p$-part was determined by Jacobson, Niedermaier and Reiner in 2003, who wrote that the other primes appear "to be difficult, due to bad behavior of its $p$-primary structure". We determine the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $K(H(d,q))$ for every prime $p$ dividing $q$ and every $d$, by an explicit rule. After the splitting of Jacobson, Niedermaier and Reiner, the group is a sum of cokernels of operators $q(c+H)+U$ on the Boolean lattice (Theorem A). These split over the indecomposable tilting modules $T(\lambda)$ of $SL_2$ in characteristic $p$ that occur in a tensor power of the natural module. The contribution of $T(\lambda)$ consists of explicit small cyclic factors and of $2^{|I|}$ large ones, where $I$ is the set of positions of the nonzero base-$p$ digits of $\lambda+1$ below the leading one. The large ones are obtained by pooling explicit integers, built from binomial valuations and base-$p$ carries, into a non-increasing sequence (Theorems I and J). The proof writes down explicit $\mathbb{Z}_p$-lattices for all tilting modules of $SL_2$, one move per base-$p$ digit; it reduces each contribution to the Smith form of an explicit $2^{|I|}\times2^{|I|}$ matrix, and computes that form as in our proof for the hypercube (The Dancing Sand Theorem), the case $p=2$. We also give closed formulas that need no pooling: for $p>d$ with ballot numbers (B), for the exponent with every prime (C), and for the number of cyclic factors (D). This proves Conjecture I of version 3 of this paper. Every result of the paper, Theorems A–J, is checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib, for every prime, and the Lean project was rebuilt from its sources on GitHub's machines, on Mathlib's published build. This work has not been refereed by a human expert.
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: Stable algebraic families of polarized dynamical systems and exceptional extensions
works.abstract: The notion of exceptional maps in arbitrary dimension was recently introduced by Ji, Song, and Xie.  In this paper, we introduce exceptional extensions of polarized dynamical systems: a family of systems admitting a positive-dimensional exceptional factor whose generic fiber dynamics have simultaneous local product coordinates with an isotrivial system. We then prove that an algebraic family of polarized endomorphisms of normal projective varieties over a quasi-projective curve is $J$-stable on a nonempty Zariski open subset if and only if it is isotrivial or it is an exceptional extension after a finite base change. This extends McMullen's theorem for stable algebraic families of rational maps to higher dimension. One ingredient is inspired by Ji and Xie's proof of McMullen's theorem: the use of homoclinic orbits and the multipliers of adjoint periodic points to control local return maps. The new ingredients are a higher-dimensional algebraization method and an inductive rigidity argument for the fiber dynamics, which together yield the exceptional extension structure.
works.subject: math.DS

works.title: Orthogonal circles and a fixed-dimensional separated-distance counterexample
works.abstract: A finite set of points in Euclidean space is distance-separated if the lengths of any two different unordered edges differ by at least one. Counting distances shows that an n-point distance-separated set has diameter at least binom(n,2), approximately n^2/2, and Erdős asked whether the diameter must be at least (1-o(1))n^2. Ho showed that the answer is no if the dimension may grow with n. The first version of this paper gave counterexamples with diameter below 0.74n^2 in a single fixed dimension. We give a sharper explicit fixed-dimensional counterexample: for every integer n at least 36354, there is a distance-separated n-point set in R^81794 with diameter strictly below (147/200)n^2 = 0.735n^2. The finite conclusion has an accompanying Lean 4 proof, including minimum distance at least one for distinct points and the actual set diameter bound. As in the first version, this construction replaces each vertex of a large macro simplex by a cluster of points. A standard Gram-deficit completion arranges those clusters on circles in mutually orthogonal planes. The arrangement makes every distance between two clusters an exact, explicit, increasing function of two digits and reduces the number of coordinates from 9m-1 to 3m-1 for m clusters. A single quadratic-residue ruler controls both the distances inside clusters and the digits between them. The proof is self-contained apart from Bertrand's postulate.
works.subject: math.MG

works.title: Subset Sum in time O(2^{0.4877n})
works.abstract:
We present a uniform randomized classical algorithm for Subset Sum with running time O(2^{0.4877n}) in the word-RAM model, for inputs whose integer bit lengths are polynomially bounded in the number n of input integers. The algorithm halts on every execution and answers correctly with probability at least 2/3.

The construction builds on OpenAI’s “Subset Sum in Time O(2^{0.49n})” (4 October 2026), retaining its framework of isolation, a capped preliminary search, a modular checksum, and alias subtraction. Two components are replaced: an alias procedure that computes phase sums using a smaller modulus, and a family of 43 checksum filters selected according to the input pattern.

The analysis combines an averaged small-layer lemma, grouping by reduced and unreduced subset sums, and rigorous numerical certificates. Verification scripts using Arb ball arithmetic check the alias constraints and 430 moment inequalities. The argument relies on results from the earlier paper, which are restated in an appendix; the numerical certificates verify specified inequalities rather than formally verifying the entire proof.
works.subject: cs.DS

works.title: The Hodge Conjecture for CM abelian varieties
works.abstract: Following the recent work [Ope26], we give a proof of the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties.
works.subject: math.AG

works.title: Sequential Games
works.abstract: We formulate a time-series game in which each player chooses a hidden Markov model (HMM) as a mixed strategy. The HMM generates a finite, variable-length sequence of probability vectors, and the payoff is assigned to the completed game as the sum of its stage rewards. We prove a conditional Nash-equilibrium existence result for games with a common finite bound on output lengths. The proof applies a fixed-point argument to the best-response correspondence when each player's admissible HMM-density set is nonempty, convex, and compact in $(L^1)$, and the completed-game payoff is bounded and measurable. A common BV bound together with $(L^1)$-closedness can ensure compactness; closure under suitable disjoint-state mixtures can ensure convexity. These properties do not follow from the HMM representation or BV regularity alone and must be verified for a specified model. Consistent estimation of HMM densities may support computation, but by itself does not establish equilibrium existence or replace the theorem's assumptions.
works.subject: math.FA

works.title: An Intrinsic Formula for the Ray–West Correction Term
works.abstract:
For a nonempty permutation $\beta$ of length $m$, let $g_2(\beta)$ denote the number of distinct permutations of length $m+2$ containing $\beta$. Ray and West showed that
$$
g_2(\beta)=\frac{m^4+2m^3+m^2+4m+4-2j(\beta)}{2},
\qquad 0\le j(\beta)\le m-1,
$$
but their correction term was not expressed as a statistic of $\beta$. This was posed explicitly as Problem 3.7 by Vatter. We give a polynomial-time formula defined entirely from $\beta$: $j(\beta)=L(\beta)+R(\beta)$, where $L$ counts licensed gaps and $R$ counts anchor-free two-deletion classes containing a collision whose canonical alignment support is a permutation interval. We also derive the Ray–West bound intrinsically and characterize its upper-bound equality cases as precisely the layered or reverse-layered permutations. The proof is combinatorial. Exact computation is used only for independent corroboration; the accompanying proof-and-replay archive contains the full proof supplement and bounded verification. This preliminary technical report was first deposited on Zenodo on August 9, 2026: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21857882.
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: $C_2$-cofiniteness of logarithmic $W$-algebras
works.abstract:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with root lattice $Q$ and lacing number $t$, equipped with an invariant bilinear form normalized so that long roots have squared length two. We prove $C_2$-cofiniteness of the
Feigin--Tipunin logarithmic $W$-algebra $\W_p(Q)$ for
$p=tm\geq2$ and $m\geq h^\vee_{{}^L\g}-1$, where
$h^\vee_{{}^L\g}$ is the dual Coxeter number of the Langlands dual.
Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction of induced affine Weyl modules gives
graded generators for the multiplicity spaces of the conformal group
action. Their degree bounds show that the intrinsic $C_2$-algebra
is a finite module over the polynomial $C_2$-algebra of its principal
invariant subalgebra. Adjoint contractions produce a finite relation
ideal in this polynomial ring. Heisenberg normal ordering and a
constant-coefficient differential equation show that its common zero
is the origin. The argument gives explicit sufficient bounds and
strong fin
works.subject: math.QA

works.title: The two-moment certificate is robust under Rudnick–Sarnak-range cubic augmentation with capacity control: An exact absorption certificate for the two-moment system at bandwidth one, with a hand-checkable witness
works.abstract:
Alpöge and Furman prove unconditionally that more than two thirds of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and lie on the critical line. Their argument rests on a two-moment certificate — the trace and the Frobenius norm of the Weil–Gabor compression, read against block structure and integrality — and that certificate is provably exhausted: within the data class (tr, Frobenius, positive-index count, integer atoms) an on-line double and a shallow off-line pair are indistinguishable, which pins the distinct-zeros optimum at $N_{d}/N = 5/6$ and the simple fraction at $2/3$. A natural proposal to break this degeneracy is to adjoin, at a second bandwidth $\lambda' = 1/2 + o(1)$ inside the Rudnick–Sarnak range, the unconditionally computable signed third trace together with two spectral-capacity rows: an all-$V$ eigenvalue-count ladder and a garnish-capacity fuzz row.

This paper proves, at the model level, and certifies computationally, that the augmentation adds exactly nothing. The marginal value of the entire cubic block over the two-moment baseline is $\delta_0 = 0$ identically, an exact LP equality with an explicit, hand-checkable witness law. It holds over the full adversary grid for the distinct-zeros benchmark ($940$ records, $|\delta_0| < 10^{-12}$ everywhere, corner $5/6$); for the simple-fraction benchmark (corner $2/3$) at its two decision cells together with cross-checks, converged clean at the stopping criterion; and inside the near-CUE data class licensed by the unconditional pair-correlation theorem of Baluyot–Goldston–Suriajaya–Turnage-Butterbaugh, where the absorption is by strict slack: there the cubic row does not bind.

The structural explanation is a set of exact identities proved here. On isolated blocks the signed cubic row is the affine function $3F - 2$ of the Frobenius row plus the second integrality level, hence blind to doubles-versus-pairs at every depth. On the $\psi_1$-zero grid the bandwidth-one Frobenius row degenerates exactly to the multiplicity count while the half-bandwidth kernel stays position-sensitive, so the cubic budget is met by arrangement at zero cost. Spectral escape is capped sharply at $2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{led}} \varepsilon_g}\,N = o(N)$, and a scalar cubic tail row with any divergent cutoff is unconditionally vacuous.

The pair-interference channel, the one gap in the atom-only model theorem, is closed by an integrality theorem throughout the admissible pair-depth family ($w \le 1$, plus deep probes at $w \in \{1.5, 2\}$): proved unconditionally for single-pair columns to $w \le 2.8$, which covers that whole family, and for multi-pair columns at $w \le 0.82$ ($w \le 0.98$ modulo one crowding cap whose ledger constant is interval-certified; on the deepest sliver $w \in (0.98, 1]$ the coverage is adversarial-numerical with the unconditional $8/9$ backstop), with an unconditional $8/9$-strength spectral backstop at all depths. Mixed-depth multi-pair columns involving the deep probes $w \in \{1.5, 2\}$ rest on that backstop together with converged adversarial pricing. The two-moment certificate, and with it the bandwidth-one ceiling, is robust under Rudnick–Sarnak-range cubic augmentation with capacity control.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Phase-Labeled Doubles and Disjoint Handleslide Cubes with Complete Markings
works.abstract: We prove two exact coherence results for marked handles in Walker's extended cobordism category.  At fixed disjoint sites, a matching pair of forward and reverse phases contributes one local $S^1\times S^2$ summand, whereas a mismatch contributes an identity cylinder.  Thus the resulting double depends only on the total Walker weight and the number of phase matches, not on the orders of attachment.  For positive handleslides supported in pairwise-disjoint protected sectors, we construct the complete marked Boolean cube and prove that every two-face commutes with weight zero; consequently, every finite route has the same composite and the endpoint identities telescope.  An optional odd-prime $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-TQFT corollary evaluates the fixed-site double as $\kappa_p^N(D_p^{\mathrm{GM}})^b$ times the identity.  Overlapping slides and their pentagon are treated by a separate companion theorem.
works.subject: math.GT

works.title: Improved Kissing Numbers in Nineteen and Twenty-One Dimensions
works.abstract: We prove that the kissing numbers in 19 and 21 dimensions are at least 12460 and 31560, improving the best published bounds 11948 (Ho) and 29768 (Cohn and Li). Both constructions start from the odd-sign configurations of Cohn and Li, which leave room around the sign vectors they add. We use this room to reshape the added vectors so that codewords closer than n/4 can be used together. In 21 dimensions each added vector has entries ±2 on one line of the projective plane of order 4 formed by the weight-5 words of the punctured Golay code, and ±3 elsewhere; a linear labelling of the codewords by lines gives 3840 new points, and the proof is by hand. In 19 dimensions we cut the 20-dimensional configuration by a hyperplane and project the sign vectors of the 20-dimensional code into it. The projections have a 16-coordinate head and a three-dimensional tail, the tails separate words whose heads are close, and one point for each of the 1792 heads with a nonzero tail can be added, where Ho adds 1280.
works.subject: math.MG

works.title: Explicit positive lower density for the Collatz Conjecture
works.abstract: Lech Mazur proved that a positive proportion of integers $n$ reach $1$ under the Collatz map in at most $10.46\log n$ steps. We give a quantitative refinement of his construction. For any $X\ge 2^{2^{2^{2^{87640}}}}$, at least $X/2^{2^{2^{87640}}}$ positive integers $n<X$ reach $1$ within $\floor{10.46\log n}$ ordinary steps, and $\floor{3.4881\log n}$ accelerated steps. We also obtain results for paths that include any prescribed integer $t$ not divisible by $3$. AxiomProver was used to obtain and formalize this result in Lean.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: A six-spin obstruction to antiferromagnetic biclique maximization
works.abstract: Sah, Sawhney, Stoner and Zhao conjectured that for every spin model whose interaction matrix has exactly one positive eigenvalue, the partition function of any graph is at most a product of biclique partition functions determined by its edge degrees. We disprove this conjecture with a strictly positive six-spin model on a triangle with three pendant edges; the violation persists on an open set of nonsingular models. The mechanism is a negative mixed covariance trace at vertices of degrees two, three and four: the triangle contributes a favourable cubic term, whereas all biclique corrections start at fourth order.
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: A cubic variance bound for matching deficiency
works.abstract: Let $M$ be a uniformly random matching of a finite graph, let $D=\nu-\mathbb E|M|$ be its expected deficiency from a maximum matching, and let $V=\operatorname{Var}(|M|)$. Kahn showed that $D$ and $V$ tend to infinity together, proved $D=O(V^4)$ when $V$ is bounded below, and conjectured $D=O(V^3)$. We prove $D\le41V+104V^2+64V^3$ for every graph, confirming the conjecture, and show that the exponent is attained by connected bipartite graphs with perfect matchings. The proof combines alternating-path identities for monomer probabilities with the sharp estimate $|V(G)-V(G-v)|\le1/4$.
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: A nonlinear connectivity code larger than every linear code
works.abstract: A connectivity code on a graph $H$ is a family of edge sets of $H$ whose pairwise symmetric differences are connected spanning subgraphs. Alon asked whether a nonlinear connectivity code can ever be larger than every linear one on the same graph. We answer this affirmatively: we construct a $4$-regular graph on fifteen vertices on which the largest connectivity code has nine members and the largest linear connectivity code has eight. The code is obtained by lifting a quaternary code of length six with pairwise agreement one through clique gadgets.
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: The Bannai–Munemasa–Venkov lattice method for strongly regular graphs: a uniform discriminant-form condition and new nonexistence results
works.abstract: Bannai, Munemasa and Venkov, and later Nebe and Venkov, excluded tight spherical designs — among them strongly regular graphs of a special kind — by studying the lattice spanned by the design: they bound its discriminant group, pass to an even (over)lattice, and compare Gauss sums by the Milgram–Braun formula. We extend this method to arbitrary strongly regular graphs with integral eigenvalues. For an integral representation G=b(A-ρ I)+cJ that is positive semidefinite with even diagonal, an elementary identity for dual vectors ties every class of the discriminant form of a maximal even overlattice to the class of a rescaled sum of the vertex vectors. This gives a necessary condition on the parameters (v,k,λ,μ) alone: a finite quadratic module with a short list of properties must exist. Its simplest case applies the textbook congruence det≡(-1)^(n/2) (mod 4) for even lattices of odd determinant to the centred representation. A sweep of Brouwer's table (v≤1300) finds 70 complementary pairs of parameter sets listed as open that fail the condition, among them (96,35,10,14), the triangle-free set (176,25,0,4) and (169,42,5,12); the grade of evidence is given for each (hand proof, or exact computation by at least two independent programs). No existing parameter set of the table fails in any representation tested, real graphs satisfy every condition with their actual discriminant forms, and the method gives short independent second proofs of the known nonexistence of srg(75,32,10,16) and srg(289,54,1,12). The simplest case also yields an infinite family: if q is a power of a prime p≡1 (mod 4) and m is odd, there is no strongly regular graph with the parameters (q^2, m(q+1), -q+m^2+3m, m(m+1)) of the negative-Latin-square type NL_m(q). This family, the parity case and the nonexistence of srg(169,42,5,12) are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib. Also deposited on Zenodo with the full data archive (the citable record): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23281359
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: Finite Analytic Characters and Tannakian Source Reconstruction: A Finite Tensor–Quiver Framework for Beyond Endoscopy
works.abstract:
This paper organizes finite tensor–quiver reconstruction for reductive source data. For a fixed reductive Zariski-closed subgroup H of a reductive complex group G and a faithful finite-dimensional representation, the standard mixed-tensor reconstruction theorem and Noetherianity imply that finitely many H-invariant tensors have common stabilizer H. Classical quiver invariant theory then implies that finitely many traces of oriented cycles separate closed orbits, including semisimple realizations.

For GL₂/ℚ, we give a restricted application of Cheng’s symmetric-square limiting distribution. After a finite-level cuspidal block has been specified and a target constituent selected by an interpolating Hecke test function built from that block’s Hecke characters, ratios of trace-formula distributions recover the first two Satake power sums at auxiliary unramified places, provided Cheng’s hypotheses hold and the full selected coefficient is nonzero. This is post-selection recovery, not a method for identifying the target constituent, and applies only to the nonzero-coefficient visible subset.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Steinhaus Piercing with Slack: The Exact Asymptotic Constant
works.abstract: Let s(d) be the largest order N for which the first n + d points of a sequence in [0,1) meet every uniform n-cell for all n ≤ N. We prove s(d) = d/(1 − log 2) + O(√d), determining the limit asked for by Anholcer et al. and disproving their conjectured coefficient. For strong piercing, which requires meeting every interval of length 1/n, we obtain an exact finite harmonic capacity and rational constructions. A Dirichlet covering lemma and a packing estimate for disjoint gaps transfer the capacity bound to ordinary grids. We also solve the finite largest-gap minimax problem, establish rigidity for infinite heap refinements, and extend the asymptotic estimate to affine arrival budgets. Ordinary near-extremizers satisfy universal laws for root sizes and first-split times, with a corresponding entropy correction. An explicit finite obstruction shows why root constraints alone do not characterize ordinary piercing.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Small witnesses for eventual Erdős--Straus binomial divisibility
works.abstract: Erdős and Straus asked whether, for each fixed $n\ge2$, every sufficiently large integer $m$ admits $1\le k\le m-n$ with $\binom{n+k}{n}\mid\binom{m+k}{k}$. We prove that it does; previously this was known only for a set of $m$ of density one. The witness can be taken with $k=O_{n,\varepsilon}(m^\varepsilon)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$: a factorial identity reduces the problem to finding a small value of a fixed polynomial coprime to $\binom mn$, which an elementary sieve provides. Conversely, the least witness is at least logarithmic in $m$ along an infinite sequence.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: A counterexample to Haglund's monotonic-zeros conjecture for the Riemann $\Xi$ approximants
works.abstract: Haglund introduced the partial sums $\Xi_N = \sum_{n \le N} \Phi_n$ of Riemann's expansion of the $\Xi$-function in incomplete gamma functions and conjectured that for every $N$ the zeros of $\Xi_N$ in the closed first quadrant, listed by increasing real part, have nondecreasing imaginary parts. The conjecture implies the Riemann hypothesis; Haglund's computations supported a weak form of it for $N \le 10$. We show that the conjecture is false for $N = 27$: $\Xi_{27}$ has a real zero in $(3144.8946, 3144.8947)$ and a non-real zero $z_0 = 3143.2206824215\ldots + 0.3152587993\ldots\, i$ in the first quadrant, whose real part is smaller. The weak form fails as well. Both facts are certified twice, independently, in interval arithmetic (Arb ball arithmetic; outward-rounded intervals with proved truncation bounds), and $z_0$ is enclosed in a square of half-width $10^{-48}$. The same violation occurs at $N = 24$ for the companion approximants $\xi_N = \Xi_N + c_N$. The failure has a mechanism: on the critical line $\Xi_N < \Xi < \xi_N$, so the real zeros of $\Xi_N$ lie in positive lobes of $\Xi$ that rise above a positive level, and a low lobe followed by a higher one near the height $4(N+1)^2$, where the approximant departs from $\Xi$, can leave a non-real zero below real zeros. The same structure shows that the number of positive real zeros of $\Xi_N$, counted with multiplicity, is odd, and that $x^2\Xi_N(x)$ tends to a negative limit on the real axis for every $N$.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: An unavoidable set of divisors for the nearest integers to ξ(3/2)^n
works.abstract: We prove that for every real ξ ̸= 0 the sequence of nearest integers [ξ(3/2)^n + 1/2], n ∈ N, contains infinitely many elements divisible by 2 or by 5. In particular, for ξ > 0 infinitely many of these nearest integers are composite. This is the nearest-integer counterpart of the theorem of Forman and Shapiro on [ξ(3/2)^n], for which Dubickas and Novikas give the unavoidable set {2, 5, 7, 11}; for nearest integers two primes suffice. The proof follows the method of Dubickas and Novikas: if 2 and 5 divide only finitely many terms, the sequence of operations is forced to become (A^2B^2)^∞, which is impossible by their Lemma 2. All results are machine-verified in Lean 4.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Non-Archimedean Massera-Schaffer-Maligranda-Pecaric-Rajic Inequality
works.abstract: Massera and Schaffer [\textit{Ann. Math. (2), 1958}] derived a breakthrough upper bound for the Clarkson angle between two nonzero vectors in a normed linear space, which was later improved by Maligranda [\textit{Am. Math. Mon., 2006}]. Pecaric and Rajic [\textit{Math. Inequal. Appl., 2007}] extended Maligranda's inequality to finitely many nonzero vectors. We derive a non-Archimedean version of  Massera-Schaffer-Maligranda-Pecaric-Rajic inequality.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Long runs and rare patterns of a random completely multiplicative function
works.abstract:
Let $f$ be a random completely multiplicative function with independent symmetric signs at the primes. We study rare constant runs and prescribed words at logarithmic lengths, despite long-range multiplicative identities. A uniform weighted two-window square-relation estimate, with critical bound $O_\varepsilon(N^{5/3+\varepsilon})$, separates exact rational relations from residual components.

At critical intensity, this estimate gives Poisson comparisons retaining positions, exact excess lengths and signs. For dictionaries, uniform bounds under size and overlap conditions are complemented by typical bounds obtained by averaging the distance after fixing the dictionary. In a quantitatively controlled regime of diverging intensity, an exact one-word coupling by largest-odd-prime pivots compares the full signed run field under prescribed small-prime conditioning. For fixed admissible window parameters and almost every fixed realization of $f$, run-start counts in prescribed near-macroscopic windows satisfy an empirical Poisson law along dyadic scales.

In the exceptionally rare regime, a relative marked comparison separates the boundary event from bulk occurrences. Conditional on existence, the first location, sign and overshoot have a two-source lattice law with scale-dependent weights. The two overshoots use different clocks: prime rank at the boundary and integer distance in the bulk.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Algebraicity of Weil classes on abelian sixfolds of Weil type for $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$ with discriminant $-2$
works.abstract: Let $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$. We prove that the Weil classes of every polarized abelian sixfold of Weil type for $K$ with Hermitian discriminant $-2$ are algebraic. This is a non-split discriminant, to which the theorems of Schoen and of Markman on split Weil classes do not apply. The proof uses Prym--Tyurin varieties of covers of $\mathbb{P}^1$ with monodromy the complex reflection group $G_{32}$, and combines known mechanisms in a new configuration. First, on every such variety the Weil classes of the six-dimensional isotypic factor are algebraic. They are obtained, by a Lefschetz-class correspondence supplied by Milne's theorem, from Schoen's algebraic Weil classes on fifty-one cyclic intermediate quotients; the choice of quotients is governed by an integral identity among characters of a torus, verified by an exact computation. Second, the ten-dimensional family of these covers dominates the nine-dimensional moduli space: we exhibit an explicit cover at which the period map has rank nine, by a certified computation. Third, a Hilbert-scheme and Baire-category argument spreads algebraicity from an open set to the whole moduli space. The discriminant of the family is identified exactly. All computations are supplied as reproducible certificates. For the members whose special Mumford--Tate group is the full special unitary group, an invariant-theoretic lemma then gives the Hodge conjecture for every power.
works.subject: math.AG

works.title: First Proof Third Batch
works.abstract:
To assess the ability of current AI systems to correctly solve research-level mathematics problems, we tested several AI systems on our ``third batch''  of ten problems in a broad range of mathematical fields; these problems arose naturally in the research process of the contributors.   This document includes the problems, our methodology, and the results of our testing. We assessed the AI-generated solutions based on mathematical correctness, quality of exposition, and quality
of attribution and citations. We provide links to supplementary documents including the human solutions, the AI-generated solutions, and the referee reports and logs for the AI-generated solutions.
works.subject: cs.AI

works.title: Marked Positive Handleslide Pentagons in Compression Bodies: Relative Coherence
works.abstract:
Let $W:X\to Y_{\mathrm{geom}}$ be a completed oriented compression body with $N\geq 3$ ordered product $1$-handles and a supplied protected three-handle sector.  We realize one positive handleslide pentagon by five diffeomorphisms with compatible complete endpoint markings.  An isotopy fixed on the entire protected boundary collar identifies the two-edge and three-edge route composites, so the comparison takes place at the level of marked maps rather than homology matrices.

The construction fixes the marked disk systems at all five vertices before choosing any edge map, so incident edges use the same endpoint data.  The cut-ball maps intertwine all fifteen disk pairings on common full-normal intervals and therefore descend smoothly through the paired faces.  Extending these quotient maps by the identity gives global representatives.  The same maps satisfy the finite compatibility conditions, including at $N=3$, when the unused-handle domains are empty but remain part of the typed construction.

The resulting boundary maps preserve the embedded meridian and product-framed dual-longitude rows, so their homological actions have blocks $M_e$ and $M_e^{-T}$ with no mixed shear.  They also preserve the same rational disk-kernel Lagrangian.  Walker's forward multiplication law lifts the relative isotopy to a literal weight-zero equality of mapping cylinders, including the seam and route weights.
works.subject: math.GT

works.title: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital nets in every dimension
works.abstract: Dick, Goda and Suzuki asked for low-discrepancy digital nets that are quasi-uniform, with minimum distance $\delta$ and covering radius both of the optimal order $N^{-1/s}$, and stated the problem as open in dimension $s\ge3$. We construct such nets in every dimension. For every $s\ge3$, every base $q$ whose prime factors are at least $s-1$, and every $k\ge1$, we give explicit digital $(0,sk,s)$-nets over $\Z/q\Z$ with $N=q^{sk}$ points, covering radius at most $\sqrt s\,N^{-1/s}$, and $\delta N^{1/s}\ge1-a^*_s/q$ once $q\ge5a^*_s+4$. The constant $a^*_s\le e^{s\log s+O(s)}$ is computed from $s$ by a deterministic polynomial-time lattice algorithm. In dimension three every $N=p^m$, $m\ge3$, is covered for each prime $p\ge37$, and, with computer assistance, every $N=2^m$ and $N=3^m$. In prime bases these families are well separated in the sense of Dick, Goda and Suzuki, and they stay so under every digital shift. One mechanism underlies all constructions. For $N=q^{sk}$ it reads as follows. The first $k$ base-$q$ digits of a point's coordinates select a cube of side $q^{-k}$, and a $(0,sk,s)$-net has exactly one point in each such cube. Digit $k+1$ of each coordinate is a linear function of the first $k$ digits of all coordinates, because the net is digital. We choose this linear function so that, between the planes where this digit wraps around modulo $q$ or where a carry occurs among the first $k$ digits, the points lie on a translate of one lattice; for the main theorem this lattice is a slightly distorted copy of $\Z^s$. All later digits move a point by less than $1/q$ of the cube side. Part~II studies the constant $K$ in $\delta N^{1/s}=1-K/q+O(q^{-2})$. We prove lower bounds on $K$ when the linear maps have bounded coefficients. At $N=q^3$ we find the optimal $K$ among nets whose points lie on lines parallel to the main diagonal. With the cube-tiling theorems of Haj\'os and Keller we show that idealized lattices with one point per cube, whose points sit independently inside their cubes, cannot exceed $\delta N^{1/s}=1$. When the positions inside the cubes are coupled, the value $1$ can be exceeded: $\delta N^{1/3}\to\sqrt{281}/16$ at $N=p^3$, $\delta N^{1/5}>1$ for $(0,5,5)$-nets from $p=37$ on, and $\delta N^{1/s}\to\min(\sqrt s/2,\sqrt2)$ at $N=p^{sk}$, which is the $E_8$ value at $s=8$ (limits as $p\to\infty$). The results are formalized in Lean~4, apart from some finite computations, which are checked by scripts.
works.subject: math.NA

works.title: Stable Algebraic Families for $\mathbb{P}^2$
works.abstract: We classify one-dimensional families of endomorphisms on $\mathbb{P}^2$ that are algebraically stable, generalizing a theorem of McMullen. The non-isotrivial families are either homogeneous lifts of flexible Lattes maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$, or a family of Lattes maps arising from abelian surfaces.
works.subject: math.DS

works.title: Another Counterexample to Little Finitistic Dimension Conjecture
works.abstract: A characteristic-zero counterexample to the Little Finitistic Dimension Conjecture is given, arguably providing a simpler variant of OpenAI's construction.
works.subject: math.RA

works.title: Unipotent tensor categories and pronilpotent Lie quasibialgebras
works.abstract:
We construct a bijection between tensor equivalence classes of unipotent tensor categories over
$\C$ and continuous Lie quasibialgebras with linearly compact pronilpotent underlying Lie algebra,
modulo continuous isomorphisms and classical twists. The bijection is defined using a fixed
universal quantization functor and solves the problem raised in Remark~4.6 of arXiv:0708.1487 by Etingof and Gelaki. The proof combines reconstruction with filtered dequantization modulo twists and
convergence of universal formulas. A category admits a tensor fiber functor precisely when a
classical twist removes its curvature.
works.subject: math.QA

works.title: The Watermark and Double Ladder Theorems: the discriminant group of the Néron–Severi lattice of a Fermat surface of prime degree
works.abstract: Let $S_m\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ be the complex Fermat surface $x_0^m+x_1^m+x_2^m+x_3^m=0$ of prime degree $m\ge 5$. Its Néron–Severi lattice $\mathrm{NS}(S_m)$ is generated by the classes of the $3m^2$ lines on $S_m$ (Schütt–Shioda–van Luijk, Degtyarev). We prove that $|\mathrm{disc}\,\mathrm{NS}(S_m)| = m^{3(m-3)^2}$ (the Watermark Theorem), which answers, for prime degree, the determinant question asked by Shioda in 1987, and we determine the discriminant group itself: $\mathrm{NS}(S_m)^*/\mathrm{NS}(S_m)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/m)^{3m^2-24m+59}\times(\mathbb{Z}/m^2)^{3m-16}$ for $m\ge 7$, and $(\mathbb{Z}/5)^{10}\times\mathbb{Z}/25$ for $m=5$ (the Double Ladder Theorem). The transcendental lattice of $S_m$ has the same discriminant group. Both proofs work with the explicit integer intersection matrix $G$ of the lines and use only elementary lattice arithmetic: the action of $G$ on functions pulled back along the $m+1$ pencils of directions of $(\mathbb{Z}/m)^2$, an explicit sublattice of $\ker G$ of index $m^{12}$, and two index computations for the order; an integer identity $GYG=6m^2G$ for the exponent, and a factorization of $G$ modulo $m$ through twelve one-variable "shadows" for the number of cyclic factors of order $m^2$. The lattice statements of both theorems are checked in the proof assistant Lean 4 with the Mathlib library, with no axiom beyond the three standard ones; the identification of $G$ with the intersection matrix of the lines is proved by hand and checked by computer. This work has not been refereed by a human expert.
works.subject: math.AG

works.title: A Positive Dispersion Optimum for the Rounded Sample Mean: Sufficiency and Necessity of Finite Variance
works.abstract:
A continuous quantity, observable only after nearest-lattice rounding, is
estimated by the mean of $n$ rounded readings of an imperfect instrument.
Averaged over the position of the true value within a rounding cell, the
mean-squared error of this estimator is a function of one dimensionless
parameter: the pre-rounding standard deviation $s$, measured in cell widths.
A perfectly repeatable instrument ($s=0$) returns the same rounded value on
every reading, so averaging provides no additional information; its
cell-averaged error is the rounding floor $1/12$. We show that this floor is
never optimal once more than one reading is taken. For \emph{any} centred
pre-rounding law with finite, non-zero variance and any sample size $n>1$,
some strictly positive dispersion yields a smaller cell-averaged error than
zero, so the global minimizer lies away from the no-scatter endpoint; and each
of the three hypotheses---$n>1$, finite variance, non-degeneracy---is
individually necessary, so existence is \emph{exactly} characterized. The
mechanism is elementary: the autocorrelation of the rounding error has a
\emph{corner} at zero lag, so a little scatter relieves the rounding bias at
first order in $s$ while its variance contribution grows only at second order.
We give the short corner-based proof and then derive the spectral form of the
criterion, using it to compute the optimum for four laws. The Gaussian
optimizer is unique and solves a Jacobi-theta equation. For the Laplace law
the bias term has a hyperbolic closed form, and the optimizer is unique and
characterized by the corresponding derivative equation. For the uniform and
two-point laws the optimizer is explicit. The uniform law cancels every bias
harmonic exactly at its first positive cancellation scale, which saturates
the natural localization bound when $n=2$; and the two-point law, whose
criterion has several local wells once $n\ge4$, shows that finite variance
ensures existence but not a single-well objective.
works.subject: math.ST

works.title: Average-radius list decoding of random linear matrix codes at rank-metric capacity
works.abstract: We show that for every fixed prime power $q$ and $0<p<1$, a uniformly random $\mathbb F_q$-linear rank-metric code in $\mathbb F_q^{n\times n}$ of rate $(1-p)^2-\varepsilon$ is, with high probability, average-radius list-decodable at radius $pn$ with list size $O_{p,q}(1/\varepsilon)$. This answers a question of Guruswami, Li and Singhal; the case $q=2$ was known. The failure probability is explicit and remains small when $\varepsilon$ depends on $n$ with $\varepsilon n^2\to\infty$. The proof combines a weighted affine extraction, span estimates for matrices from nearby rank shells, and Gaussian summation over rank profiles.
works.subject: math.IT

works.title: An Arbor Polytope with Nonreal Ehrhart Roots
works.abstract: We construct a singleton-labeled arbor on 243 vertices whose Ehrhart polynomial has a nonreal root. This disproves the conjecture that the Ehrhart roots of every arbor polytope are real and lie in $[-1,0]$. The polynomial factors as $(m+1)^{230}(7m+2)^8 f(m)/6144$, where $f$ is an explicit quintic. We derive this identity by counting lattice points for every nonnegative integer dilation, using three moments of subtree deficits. A negative value of $f'^2-ff''$ at $-3/10$ gives an exact nonreal-root certificate. The lattice-count identity and the resulting counterexample have been formalized and checked in Lean.
works.subject: math.CO

works.title: A Note on Laminar Presentations and Finite Chain Models for Ample Groupoid Homology
works.abstract: A finite free chain model for the homology of a Hausdorff ample groupoid \(G\) is cut out of the Matui complex by a finite clopen partition of each nerve space. We ask what such a model must supply and isolate three requirements: a single model that is a quasi-isomorphism, a chain of models that is a complete system with ranks and transition maps read off the presenting data, and a bound on the number of atoms in terms of the presenting cover. An \(n\)-Helly axiom on the presenting covers supplies none of them, being satisfied by every finite atomization for every \(n\), and a \(1\)-Helly family of \(N\) compact open sets can have \(2^{N}-1\) atoms. We show that a laminar presentation, a laminar basis of compact open sets in each nerve degree, supplies the third, and the second as soon as it is countable: the atoms of a finite laminar family are exactly its nonempty nodes, so a subordinate model has rank at most the number of members presenting it, the subordinate models of finite height form a complete system containing, for a countable presentation, a chain that is itself complete, and the transition maps are the least-ancestor maps of the presenting subfamilies. Every second countable Hausdorff ample groupoid admits one, and the choice is made in each nerve degree separately, laminarity not being stable under products. The first requirement is a restriction on \(G\): the homology of a model is finitely generated over a Noetherian ring, whereas \(H_0\) over \(\mathbb Z\) is not for the unit groupoid on a Cantor set or for the CAR groupoid, and a truncated model carries free homology of arbitrary rank in arbitrarily high odd degree where the groupoid has none. The chain-level statements are accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization.
works.subject: math.KT

works.title: Every nonsquare integer not equal to $-1$ is a primitive root modulo a positive lower density of primes
works.abstract: For every integer \(a\) that is neither a square nor \(-1\), we prove that a positive lower density of primes have \(a\) as a primitive root. More precisely, a zero-free half-plane \(\Re s>1-1/N\) for all Dedekind zeta functions gives a lower proportion of at least \(c_a/(N\log N)\), with \(c_a>0\) independent of \(N\ge2\). The theorem of Cureton and Thorner supplies \(N=6000\), so the positive-proportion conclusion is unconditional. The proof uses the marked Type II estimates of OpenAI to count primes $p$ such that $p-1$ is a small cofactor times one large prime. Allowing the cofactor to vary supplies an additional factor of \(\log x\) in the count. We give the counting and sieve deductions in detail and explain the dependence on the zero-free width. The argument gives a lower bound rather than the exact Artin density.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Milne's rationality conjecture
works.abstract:
We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for reductions of Hodge classes
on abelian varieties: The cohomological realizations of such classes pair rationally with Lefschetz classes (that is, classes in the algebra generated by divisor classes) in complementary codimension. The proof proceeds by establishing a dichotomy for reductions of Weil classes (an expected consequence of the rationality conjecture): Either they are orthogonal to all Lefschetz classes or are themselves Lefschetz classes. The key new input are lifting results of
Kisin--Zhou for Hodge-type Shimura varieties. This is a cleaned up version of a preprint produced and released by OpenAI on Oct 6, 2026.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: Deterministic Integer 3SUM in O(n^1.999017) Time via a Sharper Binomial-Tail Analysis
works.abstract:
We refine the analysis of the deterministic integer 3SUM algorithm of Alman and Vassilevska Williams (arXiv:2610.06783v1). Within their framework of thin matrix products and reductions through Exact Triangle, we obtain a worst-case running time of O(n^1.999017) for polynomially bounded integer inputs on a word RAM with O(log n)-bit words.

The main refinement retains the binomial tail in the preprocessing cost instead of replacing it immediately by a uniform geometric bound. An entropy estimate yields a strictly larger preprocessing saving exponent, while preserving the query algorithm and its complexity. With explicit rational parameters c = 21, theta = 0.11202, a = 0.05665, and s = 0.06945, the resulting 3SUM exponent is 1.999016414375 + o(1), giving the stated fixed exponent with a positive margin. Separately, retuning the existing analysis without the tail refinement gives O(n^1.999073).

We account for encoding, queries, prime selection, instance construction, witness scanning, and parameter rounding. The numerical inequalities are certified using exact rational interval arithmetic with explicit logarithm remainder bounds. Independent computations provide additional consistency checks. The contribution is a refinement of an existing algorithmic analysis, rather than a new matrix multiplication construction or reduction. No complete Lean formalization of the improved running-time bounds is claimed, and no global optimality or priority claim is made.
works.subject: cs.DS

works.title: A seven-eighths zero-free half-plane for unitary Weil L-functions
works.abstract: We prove that for every number field $F$ and every finite-dimensional continuous unitary representation $r$ of the global Weil group $W_F$, the $L$-function $L_F(s,r)$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re} s>7/8$, and that its only poles in this half-plane are at $s=1+it$, with order equal to the multiplicity of $\mathcal N_F^{it}$ in $r$. The analytic core is the rank-one case: $L_F(s,\psi)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re} s>7/8$ for every unitary Hecke character $\psi$ of every number field, including characters of infinite order. This extends the cubic-theta method of the OpenAI quasi-Riemann preprint, which treats finite-order characters over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, by transferring its estimates to number fields containing $\mu_{12}$ and to families of fixed infinity type, followed by an abelian descent. Brauer induction and Frobenius reciprocity then give the result in every dimension. Consequences include the same half-plane for all Artin $L$-functions and their unitary Hecke twists, an effective Chebotarev theorem, cuspidal weight-one newforms, and CM motives after the appropriate weight shift.
works.subject: math.NT

works.title: A zero-free strip for the $L$-functions of the elliptic curves $y^2=x^3+d$
works.abstract:
For a nonzero integer $d$ let $E_d$ be the elliptic curve
$y^2=x^3+d$ over $\mathbb Q$. Part I adapts OpenAI's $11/12$
argument to prove that $L(E_d,s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>17/12$.
Part II adapts OpenAI's $7/8$ argument to prove
$L(s,\overline\alpha\eta)\ne0$ for $\Re s>7/8$, where $\eta$ is any finite-order Hecke
character of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and $\alpha(n)=n/|n|$ on primary generators.
Consequently $L(E_d,s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>11/8$.
The analytic normalization is $L(E_d,s+\frac12)$, so the two boundaries
are $11/12$ and $7/8$ within $0<\Re s<1$.
The curve characters have infinite order, and require new
transformation and moment arguments. These are proved here; steps identical to
the original arguments are cited. Part II also uses the ideas from OpenAI's finite-order $7/8$
theorem.
Higher-weight and symmetric-power extensions are discussed; more general CM forms are the subject of a second paper.

works.title: Non-Archimedean Hudzik-Landes-Dragomir-Kato-Saito-Tamura Inequality
works.abstract: In 1992, Hudzik and Landes  \textit{[Math. Ann.]} derived a breakthrough generalization of the triangle inequality for two nonzero elements in normed linear spaces, which was generalized to finitely many nonzero elements independently in 2006 by Dragomir \textit{[Bull. Aust. Math. Soc.]} and in 2007 by Kato, Saito and Tamura \textit{[Math. Inequal. Appl]}. We derive a non-Archimedean version of Hudzik-Landes-Dragomir-Kato-Saito-Tamura inequality.

works.title: Gonality and quintic points on intermediate modular curves
works.abstract: For $\{\pm 1\}\subseteq\Delta\subseteq(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ let $X_\Delta(N)$ be the intermediate modular curve between $X_1(N)$ and $X_0(N)$. We determine the $\mathbb{Q}$-gonality of every strict intermediate curve $X_\Delta(N)$ with $N\le 50$, and of $X_1(N)$ for $41\le N\le 50$, where it equals the upper bound of Derickx and van Hoeij at every level. We also settle the thirty levels left open by Derickx, Hwang, Jeon and Orli\'c, completing the list of curves $X_0(N)$ with infinitely many points of degree $5$, and we show that exactly $43$ strict intermediate curves have infinitely many points of degree $5$. As a consequence, the strict intermediate curves of density degree $5$ are exactly the four $\mathbb{Q}$-pentagonal curves found by Orli\'c. The proofs use published classifications, the Castelnuovo--Severi inequality, and three computational methods; all computations can be rerun from the accompanying code.
